# An agent is built around Claude, and known by a UUID

An agent's fields are what changes how it runs, taken from what Claude Code accepts for a subagent and under Claude's names; what only labels or shows an agent goes in its `metadata`, which names `color` (one of Claude's eight) and `name`, and takes any other label as a string. Claude requires a `name`, a `description` and a `prompt` that "may be empty" ([Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#supported-frontmatter-fields)): the harness writes the agent's `id` into Claude's `name`, `description` is required here too, and there is no prompt field, since a prompt "replaces the default Claude Code system prompt entirely" ([Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents)). The `id` is a UUID version 7, which sorts by when it was made and which Bun makes natively, so renaming an agent breaks neither a session that ran it nor the memory folder Claude names after it. The optional fields are `effort`, `mcpServers`, `memory`, `model`, `role` ([ADR 0002](0002-agent-roles-main-orchestrator-subagent.md)), `skills` and `tools`. Every string and list has a minimum and a maximum and no pattern, so a value from any provider fits: the 9,165 models listed on [models.dev](https://models.dev) on 2026-10-21 are at most 79 characters as provider/model. `fallbacks` ([ADR 0003](0003-fallback-is-a-separate-agent.md)) returns when fallbacks are built.

## Considered Options

- **Claude's name as the id:** the sources call an agent's identifier its name, but a name we let people change would then have to be rewritten into every session and memory folder.
- **The 8-character id:** shorter to read, but random, so ids sort by nothing.
- **Only the fields most of the nine sources keep:** leaves out `skills` and `mcpServers`, which only three keep but which Claude takes and our agents use.
- **A pattern on every string:** the first patterns written already rejected real values, such as the provider `wafer.ai`, while the models a value goes to accept what they understand.
